theories.title: Japan bonds exit triggering global rate cut collapse
theories.summary: MarketWatch analysis reports Japan edging toward exit on buying US debt, which would impact Fed rate cut timing and retirement portfolios globally. This single central bank decision carries more leverage over US 401(k)s than Fed policy itself.
theories.why_signal: Capital flows from developed-market policy pivots can cascade into structural rate environment changes; this signals early stages of international monetary realignment.

theories.why_signal: Coordinated messaging about retirement security collapse across a major financial publication suggests narrative preparation for systemic economic weakness.
